brief.t: Good news on Kenna. Your Wednesday ten a.m. meeting happened, and Kenna has already emailed a formula for the Milk of Venus project with a thousand-unit purchase order — a live, ready-to-quote deal sitting in your inbox with the formula attached. One thing I need from you: did you also get the Atlas Eternal formula in that meeting? That's the twenty-six thousand five hundred dollar run, deposit already paid, ready to start production.

Terra Lotus, seventy-eight thousand five hundred eighty dollars and our single biggest deal, is still stuck on Aidan. He's now past two business days silent — and Kenna's own lab techs emailed yesterday saying they can't get him to respond either. I'm escalating in the priority channel at nine-thirty and I'll text you if he stays dark.

Three fresh leads landed overnight, all ready to move. Ashley Harmon at Apothik Skin wants a call on a postbiotic moisturizer and balm, one to three thousand units per SKU. Tasnim Broud at AYYUR wants prototypes and pricing on a ritual oil. And Nabil at CN1 still wants four thousand-plus lotion tubes. Ashley asking for a call is the closest thing to a booking today.
A customer's waiting on you: Raul Guardado approved the final Struck Box printing and is asking for a status update. A quick reply keeps that one moving.
The production workflow is rebuilt as a real node-and-arrow flow map and is ready for your sign-off. Say it looks right and I'll build the live CRM Production Pipeline.

The ads are still one word from you — say revert ads to manual and I flip both campaigns off Maximize Conversions. Heads-up: our Google Ads data connection is still down on a retired version, so live reporting stays dark until it's reconnected.

next: Tell me if the Atlas formula came through Wednesday — I'll log Atlas into production and set the balance follow-up
Say go and I'll build the quote for Kenna's Milk of Venus thousand-unit order
Terra Lotus — I'm escalating Aidan at nine-thirty; I'll text you if he stays silent
One word on the ads: revert ads to manual

kb.a: The Kenna meeting happened Wednesday, August twelfth at ten a.m. Afterward Kenna emailed Sam and Aidan a formula for the Milk of Venus project with a thousand-unit purchase order — the formula is attached and it's ready to quote. Still open: confirm whether the Atlas Eternal formula also came through in that meeting, which unlocks the twenty-six thousand five hundred dollar production run and advances Pure Good.

Milk of Venus is a new Kenna-referred order: a thousand-unit purchase order with the updated formula attached to Kenna's August twelfth email. Kenna asked us to re-engage them. Next step is a full quote — ingredients plus packaging, labor, and overhead — once Sam gives the go.

Sam's single lane today: confirm the Atlas formula from Wednesday's Kenna meeting, green-light the Milk of Venus quote, and give the one-word ads decision. Terra Lotus stays Aidan's lane — send nothing customer-facing until Aidan reports back.

Terra Lotus is our biggest deal at seventy-eight thousand five hundred eighty dollars, fifty-two percent of the monthly target. Aidan owns the volume-pricing conversation and is past two business days silent. Kenna's own lab techs also emailed saying they can't reach Aidan. The Consultant escalates in the priority channel at nine-thirty and texts Sam if he stays dark.

Atlas Eternal is twenty-six thousand five hundred dollars for five thousand units. The thirteen thousand two hundred fifty dollar deposit is paid; the balance is due on completion. Production kicks off the moment Sam confirms the formula is in hand from Wednesday's Kenna meeting.

Pure Good is roughly three hundred twenty-nine thousand dollars and advances off the same Kenna relationship. With the Kenna meeting now done, the next step is to schedule Pure Good's follow-up and quote.

Ashley Harmon at Apothik Skin emailed to schedule a call on a postbiotic moisturizer and balm project, one to three thousand units per SKU. She's asking for a call, which is the closest thing to a booking today — prioritize getting it on the calendar.

Tasnim Broud sent a new inbound for AYYUR, a ritual oil. She wants three prototypes plus pricing, MOQ, and production details, quoted at two hundred fifty, five hundred, and a thousand units. Qualify and respond today.

Nabil Saleh at CN1 Fragrance wants four thousand-plus eight-ounce tubes of scented body lotion and supplies his own fragrance oil. Still open to qualify — formula, packaging, and timeline toward a quote.
Raul Guardado approved the final Struck Box version-five printing and emailed asking for a status update. He's a customer waiting on a reply — close the loop today to keep it moving.
Charles Thompson at Brighten Path flagged that his beard balm and body wash samples never arrived. Carryover customer-care item — chase the shipment so it doesn't sour a live prospect.

Both net-new campaigns are on Maximize Conversions with no conversion tracking, so they're bidding blind — Contract Manufacturing CPC ran up thirty-two percent. One word from Sam, revert ads to manual, and the Consultant has the Ads Agent flip both to Manual CPC. Separately, the Google Ads data connection is down on a retired API version, so live reporting is dark until it's reconnected.

The twenty-step post-close production workflow is delivered as an eight-page PDF: a true node-and-arrow flow map plus seven role cards. It's rebuilt and waiting on Sam's sign-off; on his OK the Consultant builds the live CRM Production Pipeline.
Oreka, Nadia Dupuis, is closed and in production — eight thousand five hundred fifty-five dollars paid, thousand-unit peptide cream. Laura owns customer communication. No action needed.

The CRM browser session is logged out, which blocks live verification of developer fixes, Shopify sync, and the purchasing knowledge-base extraction. Sam logging back in as pll_tasklet_consultant unblocks all of it. No CRM developer replies came in overnight.

Victor Armendarez needs costing on two thousand units each of a curl-defining cream and an edge gel. It's overdue on Ronald's cost inputs — ingredients plus packaging, labor, and overhead before any quote goes out.

The OpenSend outbound engine is designed and waiting on Sam: buy three lookalike domains and a sending platform, create the separate Outbound Agent with its own login and memory off, and provide a booking calendar URL. Cold email only, never on the main domain; no cold texting.
Aidan's 7am Command Lab brief feed is live but Outlook-only right now because his WhatsApp and CRM are signed out on his machine. He needs to reconnect both to get the full picture.
